articles.title: The layer list
articles.summary: The layer list in the right column lists every layer of your paint. Use it to show, hide, lock, reorder and adjust layers.
articles.what: Open the layer list (right column) at the top of the right column (next to FINISHES). Each layer has a row with an eye, a lock, a thumbnail and a name. Click a name to select that layer and a card of buttons opens under it. The Actions menu holds the bigger jobs: blank layer, merge visible, flatten, Photoshop round trip and thumbnail size.
when: You opened a layered template and need to see what is in it.
You added a logo or sponsor and want to move, fade or hide it.
You need to switch the template guide layers off before you render.
how: Click the layer list at the top of the right column.
Click the eye on a row to hide or show that layer. Alt+click the eye to see only that layer.
Click a layer name to select it. Its button card and sliders appear under the row.
Type in the filter box to find a layer in a long list.
Click Done on the card, or press Esc, to deselect.

Ctrl+click names to pick several layers, then use the Merge button that shows the count.
Dragging a file onto the canvas replaces the paint. Use + Layer to add art on top instead.
pitfalls: A locked layer cannot be painted or changed. The AI copilot cannot edit it either, so unlock it first.
Hidden layers still exist. Hidden layers do not show in the render.

deep.heading: What each row shows
deep.body: Every layer row has an eye to show or hide it, a lock, a thumbnail and the name. Layers that belong to a Photoshop group sit under a group header. Click the header to collapse or expand the group, or click the eye on the header to show or hide the whole group at once. A small yellow tag on a row means one or more zones are restricted to that layer, which is handy when a finish suddenly stops showing.

deep.heading: Eye, solo and lock
deep.body: A plain click on the eye hides or shows that layer. Alt+click on the eye solos the layer so everything else disappears, and another click on the same eye restores the rest. The lock stops painting, moving and AI edits on that layer. Hidden layers stay in the file but are left out of the render.

deep.heading: Filter and thumbnails
deep.body: The filter box matches both the layer name and its group name, and a filtered list shows matches even inside collapsed groups. Actions includes a thumbnail size button that cycles through three sizes: small 24 pixels, medium 40 pixels and large 64 pixels. The choice is remembered between sessions.

deep.heading: Selecting and bulk work
deep.body: Click a name to select a layer and open its card of buttons. Ctrl+click names to pick several layers, then use the Merge button that shows the count. The Actions menu holds the document-wide jobs: blank layer, flatten, merge visible, the Photoshop round trip and thumbnail size. The small note in the menu reminds you that Ctrl+click moves a layer and a double-click opens its effects.

The group eye on the guide group is the quickest way to prepare for a render.
A yellow zone tag on a row shows which layers have zones restricted to them.
Opacity and blend mode sliders appear on the card of the selected layer.

faq.q: Why can I not paint on a layer?
faq.a: It is locked, hidden or a template guide. Unlock it by clicking the lock, and select the real artwork layer.

faq.q: What does the yellow tag on a layer mean?
faq.a: One or more zones are restricted to that layer. If the layer is hidden, those zones paint nothing.

faq.q: How do I see only one layer?
faq.a: Alt+click its eye, or use SOLO on its card. Click again to bring everything back.

faq.q: Do hidden layers go into the render?
faq.a: No. Hidden layers are left out, which is why you hide Wire and Mask before export.

faq.q: I dropped a file on the canvas and lost my paint.
faq.a: Dropping replaces the source paint. Use the + Layer button to add art on top instead.

faq.q: Can the AI copilot change a locked layer?
faq.a: No. Unlock it first. The AI can change visibility, opacity and blend mode, but never delete, merge, rename or reorder layers.

mistakes.symptom: A zone paints nothing
mistakes.cause: It is restricted to a layer that is hidden or gone.
mistakes.fix: Show the layer, or open the zone and clear its layer restriction.

mistakes.symptom: I cannot find my layer
mistakes.cause: The filter box still has text, or the layer sits in a collapsed group.
mistakes.fix: Clear the filter, or expand the group header.

mistakes.symptom: The wrong layer got edited
mistakes.cause: The previously selected layer was still active.
mistakes.fix: Click the right name first, check the card shows it, then work. Esc deselects.

protips: Alt+click on an eye is the fastest way to inspect a layer on its own.
The filter also searches group names, so typing a group name pulls up everything inside it.
Layer thumbnail size and the filter live in the same strip, so a 60-layer file stays manageable.

articles.title: What each layer is for
articles.summary: A layered template holds body paint, numbers, sponsors, tape, decals and guide layers. Knowing which is which keeps your export clean.
articles.what: A paint template (PSD) carries several kinds of layer. BODY PAINT (Car Paint) holds the livery colours. NUMBERS, SPONSORS and TAPE or stripes hold the art on top. DECALS and LOGOS (Pitbox Colors, Color Change Logos, Car_decal, Windshield Banner) hold the small stamps. TEMPLATE layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) are guides for you. They live in the group called Turn Off Before Exporting TGA.
when: You open a new template and want to know what each layer does.
You want a whole-car look on the body paint only, not on the numbers.
A number or sponsor changed colour and you need to find out why.
how: Open the layer list (right column) and read the layer names.
Hide a layer with its eye to see what it contributes.
Treat Mask and Wire as guides only. Switch them off before you render.
Put finishes on the body paint. Leave numbers, sponsors and tape as they are unless you mean to change them.
tips: Looks applied to the whole car go to the body paint layers. Numbers and sponsors stay untouched.
If you are unsure which layer holds a part, hide layers one at a time until it disappears.
pitfalls: The guide layers are not paint. If they are visible when you render, their outlines are baked into the TGA.
Layer names vary by car. Judge by what the layer shows, not only by its name.

deep.heading: How the app decides a layer's role
deep.body: The app reads the layer name and its group name. The first rule that matches wins, in this order: template guide (group name with turn off, export, template or guide, or a name with mask, wire, wireframe, mandatory, template, guide, outline or uv), then numbers, sponsors, tape or stripes, body paint (car paint, body, base paint, livery, paint, base), then decals or logos (logo, decal, banner, pitbox, windshield, sticker, badge). Anything else is other art. The AI copilot uses these roles to decide what to touch.

deep.heading: A body layer with no name
deep.body: If nothing is called body, the app falls back to the bottom-most art layer that covers a big part of the sheet and treats it as the body. This rescues files whose body layer is called something like Layer 16, but a clear name is more reliable than the fallback.

deep.heading: Typical stacking order
deep.body: The ARCA test template stacks from the bottom up as: the body base layer, White Accent, Logos, Numbers, Pitbox Colors, Car_Decal, Color Change Logos, Contingency Decals, Tape, and last the guide group holding Car Mandatory, Mask and Wire. Layers higher in the list sit in front. That order is why numbers sit on top of the body paint and tape sits on top of numbers.

deep.heading: Why roles matter for finishes
deep.body: A zone that changes the body should be limited to the body paint layer, so numbers, sponsors and tape stay exactly as they are. Whole-car looks the AI applies go to the body paint layers only. Because the role comes from the name, one oddly named layer can end up classed wrongly, so rename it before you ask for a change.

The panel is where you read names, rename and show or hide layers.
Guide layers define the paintable area, so knowing their role explains what the Mask shows.
Number and sponsor layers are the ones iRacing stamps itself, so the spec under them needs the safe material that Decal Rescue sets.

faq.q: What are Pitbox Colors?
faq.a: A decal layer in many templates. The app classes it with decals and logos because its name contains pitbox.

faq.q: Can I rename layers?
faq.a: Yes, press RENAME on the layer card. Renaming changes how the app classes the layer, so use plain words such as Body Paint or Numbers.

faq.q: A layer called Body Number is numbers or body?
faq.a: Numbers. The number rule is checked before the body rule, so the first matching word decides.

faq.q: Which layers are template layers?
faq.a: Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory and anything in a group with turn off, export, template or guide in its name. They are guides, not paint.

faq.q: Why did the AI skip one of my layers?
faq.a: It may be locked or hidden, or its name put it in a different role than you expect. Unlock it or rename it.

faq.q: What if my template has no body layer?
faq.a: The app picks the bottom-most big art layer. Rename it to Body Paint so the choice is certain.

mistakes.symptom: A whole-car look repainted my sponsors
mistakes.cause: The zone covers everything instead of the body layer, or the body layer is misnamed.
mistakes.fix: Restrict the zone to the body paint layer and rename that layer clearly.

mistakes.symptom: Guide lines show up in the render
mistakes.cause: Mask, Wire or Car_Mandatory was left visible.
mistakes.fix: Hide the guide group before rendering.

mistakes.symptom: The helper treats a decal as body paint
mistakes.cause: The name contains a body word such as base or paint, which is checked before decal words.
mistakes.fix: Rename the layer so it says decal or logo.

protips: Layer names are the app's only clue to a role, so a tidy name like Numbers or Body Paint makes every later request more accurate.
If you are unsure what a layer holds, solo it with Alt+click on the eye.
Tape is checked before body words, so a layer named Tape Body is treated as tape.

articles.title: The layer card buttons
articles.summary: Select a layer and a card of buttons opens. They copy, flip, move, merge, export or delete that layer.
articles.what: The card has one button per job. DUPE copies the layer in place. Shift+click on DUPE makes a copy shifted 50 px, handy for repeated sponsors. MIRROR copies the layer and flips it to the opposite side of the car. STROKE FX opens Layer Effects on the Stroke. MERGE down joins the layer into the one below. RENAME renames it. EXPORT saves the layer as a transparent PNG with your Hue, Sat and Bright changes baked in. MAKE ZONE builds a zone limited to the layer. DELETE removes it. SOLO shows only this layer. FLIP H and FLIP V mirror it. ROT 90 turns it 90 degrees clockwise. MOVE drags it. XFORM scales and rotates it (Ctrl+T). PAN and FIT bring it into view. LOCK ZONE ties the active zone to it (Ctrl+L). DONE deselects (Esc).
when: You need the same sponsor on both sides of the car.
You want to nudge, flip or turn a logo.
You want only that layer as a PNG to send to someone.
how: Click the layer name in the list.
Pick the button on its card.
For a flipped copy on the other side, click MIRROR and then check where it landed.
Click DONE when finished.

deep.heading: The card is two rows plus the sliders
deep.body: The first row creates things from the layer: DUPE, MIRROR and STROKE FX. The second row manages it: MERGE down, RENAME, EXPORT, MAKE ZONE and DELETE. A third group handles the view and the shape of the layer: SOLO, FLIP H, FLIP V, ROT 90, then MOVE, XFORM, PAN, FIT, LOCK ZONE, FX multiplier and DONE. The Hue, Sat and Bright sliders and the opacity and blend controls sit on the same card. A small hint at the bottom reminds you that drag or Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] reorder layers.

deep.heading: What DUPE and MIRROR name their copies
deep.body: DUPE copies the layer in place and names the copy with the word copy added. Shift+click on DUPE offsets the copy by 50 pixels right and 50 pixels down, which is handy for rows of identical sponsors. MIRROR names its copy with (mirror) added, flips it and places it at the matching spot on the other side of the sheet. Both make a normal new layer that can be moved, restyled or deleted.

deep.heading: The FX multiplier button
deep.body: The effect strength button cycles in quarter steps. Each click raises the strength by 0.25 and, once it reaches 1.5 or more, wraps back to 0.25. Shift+click resets it to exactly 1.0. It scales your layer effects (stroke, glow and the like) without opening the effects panel.

deep.heading: Locks and disabled buttons
deep.body: A locked layer greys out every button that would change it: STROKE FX, MERGE, FLIP, ROT 90, MOVE, XFORM and others. SOLO, PAN, FIT, LOCK ZONE and DONE still work because they do not alter pixels. Unlock the layer with the lock icon on its row when you need to edit it.

faq.q: Where did the FX and Flatten buttons go?
faq.a: FX is reachable by double-clicking the layer row, and Flatten moved once to the Actions menu because it affects the whole document.

faq.q: What is the difference between DUPE and MIRROR?
faq.a: DUPE copies the layer in place. MIRROR copies it and flips it to the opposite side of the sheet.

faq.q: Which way does ROT 90 turn?
faq.a: Clockwise, 90 degrees each press.

faq.q: What does MAKE ZONE do?
faq.a: It creates a zone limited to this layer's footprint. Give that zone a base material to style the layer.

faq.q: How do I reorder layers?
faq.a: Drag the row in the list, or use Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] to move a layer down or up.

faq.q: Why are some buttons greyed out?
faq.a: The layer is locked. Unlock it from its row.

EXPORT bakes in your Hue, Sat and Bright, so you can reuse a recoloured logo in another project.
DONE and Esc both deselect, which stops stray keys from editing the layer you just finished.

articles.title: Opacity, blend mode and colour tuning
articles.summary: Each layer has an opacity slider, a blend mode and Hue, Sat and Bright sliders. None of them damage your art.
articles.what: Select a layer to see them under its row. Opacity runs 0 to 100, and you can type a number in the box beside it. The Blend dropdown offers 16 modes: Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity. Hue runs -180 to 180, Sat -100 to 100 and Bright -100 to 200. These are non-destructive, so you can set them back to 0 at any time. A Color Overlay checkbox tints the layer (start colour pink-red, 50% strength).
when: A sponsor is too loud and you want it softer.
You want a shadow layer to darken what is under it.
You want to recolour a logo without repainting it.
how: Click the layer name.
Drag Opacity, or type a % in the box.
Open the Blend dropdown and pick a mode. Use Multiply to darken and Screen to lighten.
Drag Hue, Sat or Bright to tune the colour. Set them to 0 to go back.
Tick Color Overlay to flood the layer with one colour.

Heavy blend modes can change how a finish reads on the car. Check the preview.

deep.heading: What each slider does
deep.body: Opacity goes from 0 to 100 percent and you can type an exact number in the box beside the slider. Press Enter to accept it or Esc to cancel your edit. Hue turns the colours around the colour wheel from -180 to 180 degrees. Sat runs from -100 to 100, where -100 removes all colour and leaves grey. Bright runs from -100 to 200, where -100 is black and 200 makes the layer three times as bright. All three are non-destructive: setting them back to 0 restores the original pixels.

deep.heading: Blend modes in plain words
deep.body: The Blend dropdown offers 16 modes: Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity. Multiply darkens by multiplying with what is beneath, so white disappears and shadow layers sit naturally. Screen does the opposite and lightens, so black disappears. Overlay and Soft Light add contrast over what is below. Color applies only the hue and saturation of your layer, which is the safe way to recolour without losing shading.

deep.heading: Colour Overlay
deep.body: The Color Overlay checkbox floods the layer with one colour. It starts as pink-red (ff3366) at 50 percent strength with Normal blend, and you can change the colour and the amount. Because it is an effect, switching it off brings the original colours back.

deep.heading: Where the order of effects matters
deep.body: The layer is first shifted by Hue, Sat and Bright, then drawn at its opacity using its blend mode. A low opacity layer with Multiply therefore darkens less than the same layer at 100 percent. Finishes are applied on top of the composited paint, so a heavy blend mode can change how a finish reads on the car. Always check the preview.

The sliders appear on the card of the selected layer, below its row.

faq.q: Which blend mode darkens?
faq.a: Multiply. Screen lightens. Overlay and Soft Light add contrast.

faq.q: Will Hue, Sat or Bright damage my artwork?
faq.a: No. They are non-destructive. Set them back to 0 and the original comes back.

faq.q: What are the ranges?
faq.a: Opacity 0 to 100, Hue -180 to 180, Sat -100 to 100, Bright -100 to 200.

faq.q: Can the AI copilot change these?
faq.a: It can change visibility, opacity and blend mode, but not delete, merge, rename or reorder layers.

faq.q: Can I type an exact opacity?
faq.a: Yes. Type in the box beside the slider and press Enter.

faq.q: Why can I not change anything?
faq.a: The layer is locked. Unlock it from its row.

mistakes.symptom: A layer vanished after I picked a blend mode
mistakes.cause: Screen hides black and Multiply hides white, so parts of the art can drop out.
mistakes.fix: Switch back to Normal, or change the blend mode to match the art.

mistakes.symptom: The preview and my layer look different
mistakes.cause: A heavy blend mode shifts what the finish sits on.
mistakes.fix: Judge by the car preview, not the flat sheet.

mistakes.symptom: Brightness washed everything out
mistakes.cause: Bright goes up to 200 and each step is strong.
mistakes.fix: Pull it back toward 0 and add contrast with Overlay instead.

protips: Color blend mode applies only hue and saturation of the layer, so it recolours without flattening shading.
Hue and Sat are applied before the layer is drawn, so you can tint a flat logo without touching the layer itself.
Esc in the opacity box cancels the typed number and keeps the previous value.

articles.title: Layer Effects
articles.summary: Layer Effects adds a drop shadow, glow, stroke, colour overlay or bevel to a layer without changing the art itself.
articles.what: Open it from STROKE FX on a layer card. Each effect has an on or off box and its own sliders. Drop Shadow: opacity 0 to 100 (starts at 75), angle 0 to 360 (135), distance 0 to 50 (5), size 0 to 50 (5). Outer Glow: opacity 0 to 100 (80), size 1 to 50 (10), spread 0 to 100 (0). Stroke: width 1 to 20 (2), opacity 0 to 100 (100) and a position dropdown. Color Overlay: opacity 0 to 100 (50). Bevel: a direction dropdown, depth 1 to 10 (3), size 1 to 20 (5) and soften 0 to 10 (0). Clear All removes every effect. Apply keeps them. Cancel closes without keeping changes.
when: A number or logo needs an outline so it reads on a busy paint.
You want a soft shadow under a sponsor.
You want a bevelled look on lettering.
how: Select the layer and click STROKE FX on its card.
Tick the effect you want.
Set its colour, then drag the sliders and watch the live preview.
Click Apply to keep it, or Cancel to drop it.

deep.heading: Starting colours and defaults
deep.body: Each effect starts switched off with a ready colour. Drop Shadow is black at 75 percent, angle 135, distance 5 and size 5. Outer Glow is cyan at 80 percent with size 10 and spread 0. Stroke is white, 2 px wide, 100 percent, positioned Outside. Color Overlay is pink-red at 50 percent. Bevel is Up (Raised) with depth 3, size 5 and soften 0. Ticking an effect box turns it on with these numbers, so you only change what you need.

deep.heading: Order they are drawn in
deep.body: The app draws them in a fixed order: Drop Shadow, then Outer Glow, then Stroke, then Color Overlay, then Bevel last. You cannot reorder them, so choose colours with that order in mind.

deep.heading: Stroke position
deep.body: The Position dropdown offers Outside, Center and Inside. Outside adds a ring around the art and makes the letter look slightly bolder without moving the original edge. Inside keeps the ring within the original shape, so the art stays the same size. Center straddles the edge. For small numbers Outside with a contrasting colour at 2 to 4 px is the safest choice.

deep.heading: Live preview and what is kept
deep.body: While the dialog is open the canvas shows a live preview. Apply keeps the effects, Cancel (or Esc) discards changes made in this session, and Clear All removes every effect from the layer. Opening and closing the dialog without changing anything adds nothing to your undo history. Effects never change the layer's own pixels.

articles.title: Merge, flatten and blank layers
articles.summary: Merge joins layers, flatten joins them all, and a blank layer gives you clear room to paint.
articles.what: MERGE down on a layer card joins it into the layer below. Ctrl+click several names and the merge button shows the count and joins them. In the Actions menu, Merge visible (Ctrl+Shift+E) joins all visible layers into one while hidden layers survive. Flatten document puts the whole document into one layer. It first lists hidden layers and zone links that would be lost. + Blank layer adds a clear layer for the Retouch brushes.
when: The layer list is long and you want to tidy it.
You need a clear layer to paint on without touching the art.
You are done editing and want one flat layer.
how: To merge two layers: select the upper one and click MERGE down.
To merge many: Ctrl+click names, then click the merge button with the count.
To merge only what is showing: Actions, then Merge visible (or Ctrl+Shift+E).
To start fresh on a clear layer: Actions, then + Blank layer.

deep.heading: MERGE down has four conditions
deep.body: MERGE down joins a layer into the one below it, and it refuses with a message unless four things are true: there is a layer below, the upper layer is visible, neither layer is locked, and both sit in the same PSD group. If you try it across a group boundary the app stops and suggests merging inside one group or flattening. The result keeps the lower layer's place and name.

deep.heading: What gets baked in
deep.body: A merge draws both layers into one picture. Opacity, Hue, Sat and Bright changes and any Layer Effects such as strokes and shadows are painted into the pixels. The merged layer then starts clean: opacity back to 100 percent, blend mode Normal, Hue, Sat and Bright at 0, and the result is cropped tight around the art. You can no longer edit the effects separately. Zones that were restricted to the upper layer are moved to the lower one so they keep a layer.

deep.heading: Merge visible versus Flatten
deep.body: Merge visible (Ctrl+Shift+E) combines every visible layer into one and keeps hidden layers as they are. It needs at least two visible layers, stops if any of them is locked, and refuses when grouped PSD layers would break apart. Flatten document puts the whole file into one layer. It discards hidden layers, listing their names first, and clears every zone link to a layer. Because of that it shows a confirmation with Flatten Image, and tells you to use Merge Visible if hidden layers must survive.

deep.heading: Blank layers
deep.body: + Blank layer adds an empty, fully transparent layer covering the whole sheet at 100 percent opacity with Normal blend, and selects it for you. It goes on top and is the target for the Color Brush and other retouch tools. It also arrives from the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+N.

Merging moves a zone's layer link to the lower layer, and flattening removes it, so set locks after merging.
Save a project before a big merge so you can return to the separate layers.
The Retouch brushes need a layer to paint on, which + Blank layer gives you.

faq.q: Why does MERGE down say no layer below?
faq.a: The selected layer is the bottom one. Choose a layer that has another layer under it.

faq.q: Why will it not merge?
faq.a: A locked layer, a hidden upper layer, or a PSD group boundary. The message tells you which.

faq.q: Does Merge visible delete my hidden layers?
faq.a: No, they survive. Flatten does discard them.

faq.q: What happens to my zone restrictions when I merge?
faq.a: A zone tied to the upper layer is moved to the lower one. Flatten clears all zone-to-layer links.

faq.q: Can I undo a merge?
faq.a: Yes, press Ctrl+Z straight away. After many steps, the layer undo list is limited, so save a project first.

faq.q: Where is the keyboard shortcut?
faq.a: Ctrl+E merges down, Ctrl+Shift+E merges visible and Ctrl+Shift+N adds a blank layer. They work in LAYER mode.

mistakes.fix: Undo and use Merge visible instead, or set up the zone restriction again after flattening.

mistakes.fix: Merge within one group, or flatten explicitly.

protips: Save a project before merging; layer undo keeps a limited number of steps, and a saved project keeps every layer.
Hide what you want to keep apart before Merge visible. Only the visible layers merge.

articles.summary: Open Layered brings in a PSD, XCF or ORA file with its layers intact, so you can paint on the right car.
articles.what: Click Open Layered on the layer list, or the PSD/XCF/ORA button next to Source Paint. Pick the template for the same car you drive. The layer tree appears in the layer list with the guide layers inside their group. Use + Layer to add a single PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF as a new layer on top.

You got a layered paint from a friend or a shop.
You want your sponsors on their own layers.

Choose your car PSD, XCF or ORA file.

deep.heading: Which files work
deep.body: The file picker for Open Layered is titled Open Layered File and only offers .psd (Photoshop), .xcf (GIMP) and .ora (GIMP and Krita) files. A TGA, PNG or JPEG opens as a flat paint with no layers, through Source Paint. Use the template for the car you drive at its normal 2048 by 2048 size. A big PSD can take up to a minute to open, and the RENDER button wakes up when the file has finished loading.

deep.heading: What the importer tells you it skipped
deep.body: After a layered open the app can show a short note. If a layer uses a blend mode that is not supported here, it is imported as Normal and the note lists up to four names. If a layer is not made of pixels, such as a live text layer or an adjustment layer, it cannot be imported, and the note lists up to four names so you know what is missing. The picture of the whole document is also read from the file and must match its size, otherwise the open stops with an error instead of showing a wrong car.

deep.heading: Settings come back after a crash
deep.body: If the app closed unexpectedly while you were working on the same file, reopening it asks whether to restore the layer settings from before (visibility, opacity and similar). If you say yes, a message says how many layers were restored, and Ctrl+Z undoes it. The layer pixels themselves are not restored this way, so save a project when you finish a stretch of work. If the file looks different from the one you had open, the old settings are not applied and the app says so.

deep.heading: Opening starts a fresh edit history
deep.body: Opening a new layered file clears the source-pixel undo history, and zone links to layers are re-pointed at the incoming layers. Treat the open as a new starting point. Save your current project first if you want to return to it.

articles.title: Turn off the guide layers before you render
articles.summary: Mask and Wire are guides. Switch them off before every render or they end up in your paint.
articles.what: Your template comes with guide layers. Wire shows the panel outlines. Mask shows what is paintable. The group Turn Off Before Exporting TGA holds the guide layers, and Car_Mandatory sits with them. Car_Mandatory is in the same group and the support check lists it with the guides, so the group eye hides it too. While it is visible it is drawn like real art (headlight and grill mesh), so zones leave its solid pixels alone. If Wire or Mask are visible at render time, their outlines are baked into your TGA.
when: Right before you press RENDER.
Your car in iRacing shows green lines.
You hid them to judge a look and need them back for editing.
how: Open the layer list (right column).
Click the eye on Mask, Wire and Car_Mandatory (or on the group Turn Off Before Exporting TGA).
Check the preview. The outlines should be gone.

controls.effect: Shows / hides the layer. Alt+click isolates that layer.

pitfalls: Leaving even one on is enough to mark the TGA.

deep.heading: What each guide does
deep.body: Wire draws the outline of each panel, Mask separates paintable panels from dead space, the number and sponsor stamp blocks inside the Turn Off Before Exporting TGA group show where iRacing places its own elements, and Car_Mandatory (real art for the headlight and grill mesh) sits with them. All of them exist to help you paint. None is paint. A render takes the visible layers as your paint, so anything left on becomes part of the TGA.

deep.heading: Why two numbers appear
deep.body: iRacing stamps its own number and sponsors on top of your paint. If the stamp blocks from the template are left visible, they are baked into your file and the car shows two numbers or two sponsors. Wire and Mask left on show panel outlines and masks on the car. Even one guide layer left visible marks the paint.

deep.heading: One group, one click
deep.body: The guide layers sit inside one group named Turn Off Before Exporting TGA. Clicking the eye on the group header hides every layer inside it at once, which is faster than hiding Mask, Wire and Car_Mandatory one by one. In the AI copilot chat you can also say hide the template layers; Undo puts them back. The support checker shows a warning card named Template layers are switched ON and offers a one-click switch off.

deep.heading: When hiding the group changes a zone
deep.body: A zone restricted to a layer inside that group, or a layer whose parent group is hidden, paints nothing, by design. This protects you from a zone that would otherwise paint the whole car. If a zone suddenly goes blank after you toggled the group, look at which layer it is restricted to.

articles.title: The paintable area
articles.summary: The Mask layer marks what part of the sheet is really car. Paint outside it never reaches the car.
articles.what: The template sheet is mostly dead space between the car panels. The Mask layer marks the paintable panels as clear and the rest as solid. There is no layer group called Paintable Area; the layer is simply named Mask. The app uses the mask to know what counts as car when it reads parts, builds zones and previews.
when: You wonder why paint outside the panels does not show.
The AI copilot asks about parts and the mask.
A zone seems to cover less than you expected.
how: Open the layer list (right column) and find the layer called Mask.
Turn it on to see which parts are paintable.
Turn it off again before you render.
tips: Use the Mask layer view to check how a zone sits in the panels.
Dead space can look odd on screen. It is not part of the car.
pitfalls: The mask guide must be off for the export.
A wrong template for your car gives a wrong mask.

deep.heading: How the Mask is read
deep.body: On the template Mask layer, clear pixels are paintable panels and solid pixels are dead space. The app reads it that way and accepts it only when the paintable share is between 8 percent and 92 percent of the sheet. If less than 12 percent of the Mask is solid, the app assumes it was drawn the other way round and flips it.

deep.heading: Mask plus Wire gives you separate panels
deep.body: The Wire layer draws a green outline around every panel. The app thickens those outlines by one small block, removes them from the paintable area, and counts each remaining clear piece as one panel. That is how it tells the hood, roof and sides apart. If a dense Wire mesh would shatter the panels, so that the split keeps under 70 percent of the paintable area, it separates panels by trimming thin bridges instead.

deep.heading: No Mask layer on the sheet
deep.body: A flat paint file with no Mask can still work. If the sheet still shows the template dead-space tone, or transparency, everything else counts as paintable. If it shows neither, the app falls back to the footprint of the body paint layers, which only splits panels that have empty space between them.

deep.heading: What it changes in practice
deep.body: Shokker AI looks that cover the whole car, and an Everything zone made by the copilot, use the paintable area as their region, so dead space is left alone. The app also stores a coarse 32 by 32 fingerprint of the paintable area to recognise the same car template again. Mask and Wire are guide layers, so they are ignored when the app works out which zone owns which paint.

faq.q: Why is half of my sheet solid or dark?
faq.a: That is dead space between the car panels. It is not part of the car, so nothing you put there reaches iRacing.

faq.q: Does paint in the dead space show on the car?
faq.a: No. Only the clear panels on the Mask map onto the car, and with Mask hidden the dead space simply shows your base colour, which iRacing never displays.

faq.q: How does the AI copilot know where the car is?
faq.a: It reads the Mask layer first, then splits it by the Wire outlines. Without a Mask it uses the template dead-space tone, then the body paint layers.

faq.q: My Mask looks inverted. Is that a problem?
faq.a: No. If under 12 percent of the Mask is solid, the app reads it the other way round automatically.

faq.q: Can I keep Mask on while I paint?
faq.a: Yes, it is only a guide. Switch it off before every render, or the mask is baked into your paint.

faq.q: A wrong template gives a wrong result. Why?
faq.a: The app maps parts from the template of the car you loaded. If it is not the template for the car you drive, the panels it finds are not your car's panels.

mistakes.fix: Turn both off, or hide the whole Turn Off Before Exporting TGA group, then render again.

mistakes.cause: The sheet comes from a template for a different car, or the Mask was removed

Both a Mask and a Wire layer give the best part detection, because the Wire outlines separate panels that the Mask alone joins.

articles.title: Wire, Mask and Car_Mandatory
articles.summary: These three template layers help you paint. Wire outlines each panel, Mask shows what is paintable, Car_Mandatory shows required items.
articles.what: Wire draws green outlines around each panel. Mask separates paintable panels (clear) from dead space (solid). Car_Mandatory is real template art (the headlight and grill mesh), so it is part of the car and is not just a guide. They sit in the group Turn Off Before Exporting TGA. They are not paint. They help you see where things go.

You want to know which area is paintable.

how: Turn Wire on to see panel outlines while you place a logo.
Turn Mask on to see paintable and dead areas.

deep.heading: Three guides, three jobs
deep.body: Wire draws each panel outline in bright green, and the lines between them in the mesh are white or grey. Mask is the paintable map: clear is panel, solid is dead space. Car_Mandatory sits in the same group and carries real template artwork such as the headlight and grill mesh, which is why the group is named Turn Off Before Exporting TGA. None of the three is your paint, so all of them go off before you render.

deep.heading: How the app finds them
deep.body: The app treats a layer as a template guide when its own name, or the name of its group, contains words such as mask, wire, wireframe, mandatory, template, guide, outline or export. So a renamed layer such as Mask copy is still treated as a guide, and the AI copilot lists it as template, switch off before exporting.

deep.heading: Why the AI copilot wants Wire and Mask
deep.body: The Mask says where the car is and the Wire outlines say where one panel ends and the next begins. With both, the AI separates the hood, roof and sides cleanly. Without Wire it has to split panels by trimming thin bridges in the Mask, which is less exact.

deep.heading: Your choice, not the app's
deep.body: The AI copilot chat can hide or show the guides for you: say hide the template layers, or show the template layers. It cannot delete or rename layers. Undo puts back what the answer changed.

deep.heading: How zones treat them
deep.body: When the app works out which zone owns which paint, a layer whose name starts with Mask or Wire never blocks anything, so a zone can still claim the paint underneath. Car_Mandatory is not exempt. It counts as real art on top, so a zone does not repaint the grill area it covers.

faq.q: Are Wire, Mask and Car_Mandatory part of my paint?
faq.a: No. They help you see where things go. If they are visible when you render, they are baked in.

faq.q: Which one gives me two numbers on the car?
faq.a: The number and sponsor stamp blocks in the Turn Off Before Exporting TGA group. iRacing stamps its own on top, so a visible block doubles them.

faq.q: Can the AI copilot turn them off for me?
faq.a: Yes. Say hide the template layers. It switches them off and Undo brings them back. It can also check this in the setup check and offers a one-click switch off.

faq.q: Do I need the Wire layer?
faq.a: Not to paint. It helps you place art, and it gives the AI exact panel walls. Without it the app still splits panels from the Mask, just less exactly.

faq.q: I turned the guides off and the sheet looks different. Is something wrong?
faq.a: No. With Mask off, the dead space between panels shows your base paint colour. That area is not on the car.

faq.q: Why does a layer I renamed still count as a guide?
faq.a: The app goes by words in its name or its group name, such as mask, wire or guide, and not by the layer position.

articles.title: Lock a zone to a layer
articles.summary: Make a zone act only on one layer. Its look then stays on that layer and on nothing else.
articles.what: Select a layer, then click LOCK ZONE (or press Ctrl+L) to tie the active zone to that layer. The zone then owns pixels only where that layer is solid (alpha 128 or more) and the art above it is not (alpha under 128). MAKE ZONE does the same in one step: it makes a new zone limited to the layer, and you then give it a base material.
when: You want a sponsor or number to have a different finish from the paint.
A finish bleeds onto art you did not want it on.
You want one logo in chrome and the rest in gloss.
how: Select the layer in the layer list.
Click MAKE ZONE for a new zone, or select an existing zone and click LOCK ZONE.
Give the zone a base material.
Check the preview. The finish should sit only on that layer.

deep.heading: Two ways in, one result
deep.body: MAKE ZONE on a layer card creates a new zone named after the layer with the word zone added, set to Everything, hard edge, restricted to that layer. It has no base material yet, so it paints nothing until you pick one. LOCK ZONE, or Ctrl+L, takes the zone you already have selected and restricts it to the selected layer. Both are one undo step.

deep.heading: Lock replaces, it does not add
deep.body: LOCK ZONE sets the zone to exactly that one layer and drops any earlier layer restriction on the zone. To restrict one zone to several layers, use RESTRICT TO LAYERS in the zone panel, which combines the layers into one area. Without a selected layer you get the toast No layer selected, and without a selected zone you get Select a zone first.

deep.heading: Exactly which pixels the zone owns
deep.body: The zone owns a pixel when the layer is at least half opaque there, counting the layer opacity, clipping and visible effects, and the art stacked above it is less than half opaque. There are no fractions and no feathered edge. A fully opaque layer at 40 percent opacity does not count, while one at 50 percent does.

deep.heading: Order, hidden layers and leftovers
deep.body: Zones claim pixels in list order, top first. A pixel covered by art above the layer goes to the zone for that art, or to Everything Else when nothing claims it. If every layer a zone is restricted to is hidden, the zone owns nothing and a message tells you why instead of silently painting over hidden art.

faq.q: What is the difference between MAKE ZONE and LOCK ZONE?
faq.a: MAKE ZONE creates a new zone restricted to the layer. LOCK ZONE restricts the zone you already have selected.

faq.q: Is there a shortcut?
faq.a: Yes, Ctrl+L locks the selected zone to the selected layer. It does not fire while you are typing in a box.

faq.q: My new zone paints nothing. Why?
faq.a: A new zone from MAKE ZONE has no base material. Pick one in the zone panel.

faq.q: Can a zone be locked to two layers?
faq.a: Not with LOCK ZONE, which keeps one layer. Use RESTRICT TO LAYERS to pick several.

faq.q: Will the edge be soft?
faq.a: No. Layer locked zones use a hard 50 percent line, so the edge is clean with no halo.

faq.q: I hid the layer and the zone stopped. Is that a bug?
faq.a: No. When all the zone's layers are hidden it owns nothing, by design. Show the layer again.

articles.title: Photoshop round trip
articles.summary: Send the finished paint and spec to Photoshop as named TGA files, edit them there, and bring the result back.
articles.what: Open the Actions menu and choose Photoshop round-trip. Type a car file name in the first box and choose an export folder in the second. Click Export. The app writes the finished paint as a TGA, a Spec TGA, four separate channel TGAs and a manifest into that folder. It does not write your layers. Edit the files in Photoshop, then bring a TGA back through Settings, Import Spec Map (Merge Mode), Import TGA.

A friend edits your layers in another tool.
You need the paint and the spec channels as separate TGA files.

Pick Photoshop round-trip.
Type a name such as your car and a number in the file name box.
Choose or paste the export folder.

deep.heading: What it writes
deep.body: It does not export your layers. It runs the same work as a render and writes finished files into a folder named after your car file name, inside the export folder you chose: the paint as a TGA named after your car, the spec map as the same name plus Spec, and separate TGAs for the spec channels metallic, roughness, clearcoat and mask, plus a copy of the base paint. A manifest file in the same folder lists them. The app also remembers which export was last.

deep.heading: Name and folder rules
deep.body: The Car file name box must not be empty or you get Enter a car file name. Any character other than a letter, digit, dot, underscore, hyphen or space is replaced by an underscore. The Export folder box fills itself with the last folder you used, or otherwise with a PhotoshopExchange folder inside ShokkerPaintBooth in your Documents. Source Paint must be set in the header bar, or a flat image must be open, or you get a message to set it.

deep.heading: What goes into the paint
deep.body: Decals with their own spec finish, and spec stamps with their finish, are included. With layers loaded and no decals, the app sends the live canvas as the paint, so your layer work is not dropped. The export needs the engine to be online, otherwise it shows the engine offline message.

deep.heading: Bringing it back
deep.body: Open the spec in Photoshop, save, then use Settings, Import Spec Map (Merge Mode), Import TGA. Zones paint on top of the imported spec. Areas no zone covers keep the imported spec. A zone set to Everything or Remaining covers the whole imported spec, so keep those off while you rely on your edits.

faq.a: No. It writes the finished paint and spec as TGA files. Use the EXPORT button on a layer card for a single layer as a PNG.

faq.q: Where do the files go?
faq.a: Into a folder named after your car file name, inside the Export folder box. The box remembers the last folder.

faq.q: Can I use these TGAs on Trading Paints?

faq.q: Which spec channel does clearcoat use?

articles.title: Decal Rescue kit
articles.summary: Decal Rescue makes numbers and sponsors look like real vinyl: flat, satin or gloss, and not shiny like the paint.
articles.what: In the Decal Rescue kit you pick a vinyl type. Flat Vinyl uses metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 110. Satin Decal uses metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 75. Gloss Decal uses metal 0, roughness 42, clearcoat 22. The workflow is to draw the footprint of the number or sponsor, then use Mask, then Grow, so the finish covers the edges.
when: A number looks like it is part of the paint and you want it to look like a sticker.
The decal edge shows a halo of the base finish.
You want sponsors to be matte on a gloss car.
how: Open the Decal Rescue kit.
Draw over the number or sponsor to mark its footprint.
Use Mask, then Grow, to cover the edge.
Pick Flat Vinyl, Satin Decal or Gloss Decal.
Check the preview.
tips: Gloss Decal has the lowest roughness, so it looks nearest to the car paint.
Decal Rescue needs a drawn selection on the active zone, so draw the footprint first.
pitfalls: A footprint that is too tight leaves a rim of the base finish.
Decal Rescue replaces the active zone's whole recipe and clears its layer restriction, so use a zone of its own for the decal.
aliases: numbers hard to read under chrome

deep.heading: Why it exists
deep.body: Sim-stamped numbers and sponsors take on the spec map underneath them. Over chrome, candy or metallic bodywork a white number can turn into a mirror and become unreadable. Decal Rescue sets a safe, non-metallic spec under the stamp footprint and leaves the paint colours alone. Open it from MASK > Advanced spec utilities, then Decal Rescue Kit.

deep.heading: The three presets in numbers
deep.body: Flat Vinyl is metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 110. Satin Decal is metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 75. Gloss Decal is metal 0, roughness 42, clearcoat 22. The spec alpha is set to 255. On the clearcoat channel 16 is maximum gloss and 255 is dull, so 22 is almost full gloss, 75 is a soft sheen and 110 is flat.

deep.heading: What it does to the zone
deep.body: It works on the active zone only and needs a selection in it. It sets the zone base to a flat Foundation material, keeps the source paint colours, and clears every pattern, overlay and extra base on that zone. It also clears any layer restriction so the exact footprint you drew is what reaches the spec. One Undo restores the zone's previous recipe.

deep.heading: What stops it
deep.body: With no selection in the active zone you get a message to draw the number or sponsor footprint first. If the zone has its Base, Pattern or Intensity locked, you must unlock them first. If the zone has a layer restriction, the kit shows a note that Rescue will clear it.

faq.q: Does it change my colours?
faq.a: No. The zone keeps the source paint colours and only the spec under the footprint changes.

faq.q: What do M, R and CC mean in the kit?
faq.a: Metal, roughness and clearcoat. They are values from 0 to 255 in the spec map.

faq.q: Nothing happens when I open the kit.
faq.a: You need an active zone with a drawn selection. Draw the number or sponsor footprint first.

faq.q: It says to unlock my zone.
faq.a: The zone has Base, Pattern or Intensity locked. Unlock them, then apply.

faq.q: Can I undo it?
faq.a: Yes. One Undo restores the zone's earlier recipe.

faq.q: Does it touch my layers?
faq.a: No. It leaves all layer pixels alone. It does clear the zone's layer restriction.
